user.title: Connect to your MySQL Database
user.description: Please enter the connection details. Note: Setting the Row Limit above 1000 is at your own risk and may impact performance.

data_description.mysql_use_tls: Encrypts the traffic to the database. The server must have TLS configured; the connection fails if it does not. The server certificate is not verified, so this protects against reading along on the network, not against a server impersonating yours. Off by default so existing setups keep working.
data_description.mysql_readonly: Refuses the Execute action on this connection, whatever the statement says. Use it for a connection that only feeds dashboards or reports, so a write aimed at the wrong connection cannot land here. Off by default.

error.cannot_connect: Failed to connect to the server. Check the host, the port and your firewall. Details: {error}
error.invalid_auth: The server refused the username or password.
error.unknown_database: The database does not exist, or this user has no access to it.
error.tls_unavailable: The server accepted the connection but did not encrypt it. Configure TLS on the database, or turn the encryption option off.

execute.name: Execute
execute.description: Runs a statement that changes something (INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, DDL, and maintenance statements such as ANALYZE or OPTIMIZE) and returns what it affected. Refuses a statement that only reads; use Query for that.

values.name: Values
values.description: Optional list of values for the %s placeholders in the query, in the order the placeholders appear. Templates are rendered with their native type.

db4query.name: Database for query
db4query.description: Optionally override the database name for this specific query.

config_entry.name: Connection
config_entry.description: The database connection to run this query on. If left empty, the default instance will be used.

raise_on_error.name: Raise on error
raise_on_error.description: Stop the caller with an error when the statement fails, instead of reporting it in the response as succeeded false. Off by default for this action; switch it on to get the behaviour Query has.

query.name: Query
query.description: Runs a statement that only reads - SELECT, WITH, SHOW, DESCRIBE, EXPLAIN and the like - and returns the rows together with the metadata about the result. Refuses anything that changes data or schema; use Execute for that.
